I'm interested in applying machine learning and protein modeling in terms of bioinformatics, and I like working on finding computational solutions to problems in disease research. - my work often involves combining science research with entrepreneurship with public policy. i've worked on three entrepreneurial projects over the course of my undergrad journey and founded ventures across edtech, biotech, and healthtech that have been accepted into programs like Big ideas, NSF I-Corps, Berkeley StEP (student entrepreneurship program), eHUB, and for this upcoming fall semester, Skydeck Pad-13.

I am obsessed with the brain in ways that probably warrant concern. Specifically, I care about the use cases of computational biology with neuroscience/biotech, applied to things ranging from the aging brain, neurodegeneration, gene therapies, therapeutics, neurotech, and even how we get drugs to cross the blood-brain barrier to treat things like Alzheimer's. This summer I was at MIT Lincoln Laboratory building tools to map subcortical structures implicated in consciousness and affective experience. I previously was Project Lead for two semesters in CB@B's founding cohort, leading an academic project and two subprojects with NeuroAge (building aging clocks and doing drug discovery).

Beyond research, I have been dancing Bharatanatyam since I was five years old and am now competing in the collegiate desi dance circuit with Natya! I am also involved with Neurotech@Berkeley. I do Carnatic classical vocals, guitar, violin, and have a YouTube channel where I post singing covers. I like to cook, make fancy coffees with my espresso machine, hike, sew clothes, and am in love with fashion and couture! I also recently got into writing Substack articles!
I'm interested in agents, lab automation, and large neural nets for biology.
